printed_headline_estimate: N = 240 households (2019-2020 survey, p. 8). Binary logistic regression for own in-home financial water access (p. 13, Table 1 & Table S3): Omnibus chi2 = 88.314, p < 0.001; income < INR 10,000 vs > INR 20,000 OR = 0.075, p = 0.001 (bivariate income chi2(2) = 54.319, p < 0.001, Cramer's V = 0.476). Binary logistic regression for reliance on public water sources (pp. 14-15, Table 2 & Table S4): Omnibus chi2 = 82.423, p < 0.001; income < INR 10,000 vs > INR 20,000 OR = 8.319, p = 0.004 (bivariate income chi2(2) = 52.044, p < 0.001, V = 0.466; caste and occupation non-significant after adjustment). Kruskal-Wallis H tests across occupation, income, caste, education, and household size for ordinal access/barrier items (Tables 3-7, pp. 15-18), e.g., perceived local institutional role by caste H(3) = 13.749, p = 0.003, epsilon2 = 0.058 (Table 6, p. 18) and social dominance/untouchability by caste H(3) = 30.341, p < 0.001, epsilon2 = 0.127 (Table 7, p. 18).
publication_year_note: Printed header on pp. 1-36 states 'SN Social Sciences (2026) 6:371', 'Received: 30 March 2026 / Accepted: 18 August 2026', and copyright 2026 (only 2026 appears on the PDF).
rationale: Although the paper reports inferential quantitative tests on a 2019-2020 survey of N = 240 households (Pearson chi-square, binary logistic regressions, and Kruskal-Wallis H tests with Dunn-Bonferroni post hoc comparisons in Tables 1-7, pp. 13-18), every single inferential model tests only household socio-demographic predictors (monthly income, occupation, caste group, educational attainment, and household size) rather than a rule-type legal, tenure, tariff, ownership, regulatory, or governance-arrangement exposure (failing narrow Criterion 2). In Table 6 (p. 18), 'Local institutional role in public water service provision' is a respondent perception item compared across socio-demographic groups rather than an institutional exposure tested on a household water access outcome, and all examination of Gram Panchayat/Block/PHED governance processes and 2023-2024 JJM solar-powered community taps is purely qualitative (pp. 9, 18-25, 32).
